Modern.brandNameRationale: Brick is the building material; loam is the soil. Paired they reference both the building and the land. Two-noun & paired naming follows the considered real-estate school (Compass and Side register).
Modern.industrySummary: Modern real estate has been moving from agent-led to platform-led, with the customer doing more of the discovery work themselves. The opening is for a brand that respects the buyer as a design-literate adult and treats the agent as a real, accountable person.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Compass (compass.com) holds the modern tech-led peer position. Side (side.com) sits in the agent-platform tier. Zillow (zillow.com) does the consumer marketplace middle. We sit closer to Side in posture, with a sharper consumer brand.
Modern.positioningStatement: A modern brokerage with named agents, clean listings, and no broker speak.

targetAudience.primary: 30 to 55. Buying their first or second home. Has done the research. Wants an agent who will tell them when a house is wrong for them.

Photograph the actual house, not the lifestyle
Speak to the buyer as an adult

customSections.title: Where it lives

Brick & Loam delivers by:

Modern.tagline: A brokerage for the long calendar.
Modern.brandNameRationale: Hartsfield is a real English-origin surname with a property-and-trade register. Realty is the heritage brokerage suffix. Single-surname + Realty follows the regional brokerage convention.
Modern.manifesto: Real estate runs on urgency. New listing! Just hit market! Three offers already! We started Hartsfield Realty because the urgency is mostly manufactured and the decision is mostly not. The right house is rarely the one you can see today. Most of our work is the year before the purchase. We are happy to be the friend you talk to for twelve months before you actually buy anything.
Modern.industrySummary: Brokerages compete on listings and speed. There is a smaller opening on the buyer side — a brand that markets to the eighteen months before the purchase and treats long research as the product. Compass-style premium broke ground here; nobody has taken it further.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Compass (compass.com) defines the upscale modern brokerage. Side (side.com) holds the agent-platform position. The Agency (theagencyre.com) sits in the boutique premium slot. We compete on time horizon, not transaction speed — a different axis entirely.
Modern.positioningStatement: Hartsfield Realty is a brokerage that works on the eighteen-month timeline most buyers actually live on.
Modern.positioningRationale: We bill our patience instead of hiding it. The pre-purchase year is the product: market notes, neighborhood walks, financing prep, off-market intros.

targetAudience.primary: Buyers 30–55 who have decided they will move within two years but do not feel rushed.
behaviors: Save listings they will not act on for months.
Walk neighborhoods on weekends.
Read the local newsletter and zoning notes.
Have a number in mind and ignore it.
motivations: Want to learn the market before they move.
Want an agent who is not pushing them.
Want to be ready when the right house appears.

dos: Talk about time first — 'in about eighteen months'.
Reference the customer's stated timeline back to them.
donts: No countdown timers on the site.
No surprise calls about a 'hot new listing'.

messagingPillars.name: The eighteen-month plan
messagingPillars.description: We start with a written plan for the year-and-a-half before you buy: financing, neighborhoods to walk, market triggers to wait for, sellers to keep an eye on.

messagingPillars.name: Neighborhood notes
messagingPillars.description: Monthly note per neighborhood you are tracking — price moves, what sold, what is sitting, what is coming. Plain numbers, no spin.

messagingPillars.name: The right house, not the next house
messagingPillars.description: We are happy to tell you to wait. Our incentive is the right transaction, not the next one. If we do not have the right house this quarter, the answer is to keep walking.

Modern.brandDescription: Plot & Parcel is a modern small brokerage specializing in residential land transactions, lot-and-build sales, and considered single-family-home brokerage in growing residential markets.
Modern.scope:
Plot & Parcel works across:
• Residential land sales and lot-and-build transactions
• Single-family-home brokerage in growing residential markets
• Custom-build coordination between buyers and architects
• Direct relationships with regional residential developers
• Annual market letter for past and prospective clients
Modern.mission: To run a modern brokerage focused on residential land, lots, and the relationship between the buyer and the build.
Modern.vision: A brokerage whose growing residential markets are well-served because we know the land and the builders.
coreValues: Considered — land first, then the build.
Modern — small brokerage with land discipline.
Specific — every lot publishes utilities, zoning, suitability.
Warm — the coordination is the relationship.
Modern.brandNameRationale: Plot and Parcel are the two foundational real-estate trade words for a defined piece of land — used historically across British and American property law. Paired they ground the brand entirely in the residential-land vocabulary. Two-noun & paired naming follows the considered-modern real-estate school (Brick & Loam, Heath & Hound register).
Modern.manifesto: Most modern brokerages chase listings in existing housing stock. We started Plot & Parcel because the actual interesting work in growing residential markets is the land itself — the plot, the parcel, the lot-and-build. We work with buyers, builders, and architects from the land purchase forward.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern brokerage has converged on existing-home transactions. The opening is for a small brokerage that competes on residential land and lot-and-build expertise in growing markets — closer in spirit to a heritage land brokerage than to a modern listing-driven firm.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Compass (compass.com) plays the modern brokerage reference at scale. Side (side.com) holds the agent-platform peer slot. The Agency (theagencyre.com) sits in the boutique-modern peer position. Coldwell Banker Land Specialists (coldwellbanker.com) plays the legacy land peer reference. We belong with a small modern land-focused brokerage tradition.
Modern.positioningStatement: Plot & Parcel is a modern small brokerage specializing in residential land, lot-and-build sales, and single-family-home brokerage in growing residential markets.
Modern.positioningRationale: We compete on land-and-build expertise. The brokerage works with buyers from the lot purchase through the build coordination.

targetAudience.primary: Buyers planning to build single-family homes in growing residential markets, regional residential developers, and architects coordinating client builds.
behaviors: Buy residential land for build-to-suit projects.
Coordinate with architects and builders across multi-month projects.
Care about land suitability, utilities, and zoning.
Maintain relationships with brokers across multiple builds.
motivations: Want a brokerage that knows land and builders.
Want coordination from lot purchase through build.
Want a small brokerage with land expertise.

dos: Lead with the land and the build coordination.
Publish lot listings with full utility, zoning, and suitability information.
Reference architects and builders by name.
Sign correspondence by the principal broker.

messagingPillars.name: Land and lot expertise
messagingPillars.description: Every land listing publishes full utility, zoning, and suitability information. The brokerage's primary expertise is in residential land.

messagingPillars.name: Build coordination
messagingPillars.description: We coordinate between buyers, architects, and builders from lot purchase through home completion. The relationship spans the build.

messagingPillars.name: Annual market letter
messagingPillars.description: Once a year the brokerage publishes a letter on the residential markets we serve — land prices, build costs, zoning changes. The letter is the marketing.

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark — Plot & Parcel set in a calm modern serif with a long ampersand. A small lot-map mark sits above the wordmark on listings.

colorPalette.name: Land
colorPalette.meaning: Primary — the colour of a working land parcel.

colorPalette.name: Sky

typography.secondary: A book serif for the annual market letter.
typography.rationale: Two related serifs. The brand reads like a careful real-estate publication.

Modern.brandDescription: Meridian & Vue is a boutique luxury residential brokerage specializing in homes priced above $2M across primary and resort markets. The firm pairs a small bench of senior agents with concierge-grade marketing, private-client discretion, and an off-market network. It positions itself as an advisory house for trophy property rather than a transaction mill.
Modern.scope: A full brand system covering wordmark, listing-collateral suite, private-client deck, signage, and a tech-forward web presence with cinematic property pages. The engagement also defines voice for off-market 'whisper listings' and an invitation-only buyer database.
Modern.brandNameRationale: 'Meridian' evokes the surveyor's reference line and a peak position; 'Vue' nods to the view premium that defines luxury value. Together they read as coordinates for a singular address.
Modern.industrySummary: In 2025 the ultra-luxury tier ($2M+) has decoupled from the broader market: while 30-year rates hovering near 6.7-7% chilled mid-market activity, high-end buyers transact in cash and are far less rate-sensitive. Luxury inventory rose modestly as sellers tested pricing, lengthening days-on-market and shifting leverage toward qualified buyers. Wealth migration into Florida, Texas, and mountain-resort markets continued to reshape where trophy demand concentrates.
Modern.competitorLandscape: The Agency (theagencyre.com) leads with a lifestyle-media model; Compass (compass.com) wins on agent-tech and scale; Douglas Elliman (elliman.com) anchors legacy luxury in the Northeast and Florida. Meridian & Vue differs by staying deliberately small and advisory, emphasizing off-market discretion over volume marketing.
Modern.positioningStatement: For principals who treat property as portfolio, Meridian & Vue is the discreet luxury brokerage that advises rather than sells.
Modern.positioningRationale: Ultra-high-net-worth sellers fear exposure and overexposure equally; an advisory, discretion-first stance differentiates from media-heavy luxury brands. Scarcity of agents signals exclusivity, which itself is a luxury value driver.

targetAudience.primary: Ultra-high-net-worth individuals and family offices aged 45-70 transacting $2M-$25M residential assets. They are time-poor, privacy-obsessed, and relationship-driven, often buying a second or third home. They expect white-glove service, value discretion over flash, and make decisions with advisors (attorneys, wealth managers) in the room.
behaviors: Request off-market and pre-market access before public listing
Vet agents through referral networks rather than ads
Negotiate in cash or with portfolio-backed financing
Expect NDA-level confidentiality on transactions
motivations: Protect privacy and reputation
Acquire scarce, status-defining assets
Optimize property as part of a wealth portfolio

Modern.mission: To advise discerning principals on the acquisition and disposition of exceptional homes with absolute discretion and uncommon judgment.
Modern.vision: To become the most trusted private-client name in luxury residential real estate across the world's premier markets.

messagingPillars.name: Advisory, not transactional
messagingPillars.description: We counsel clients on timing, pricing, and portfolio fit. The sale is the outcome of good advice, not the goal.

messagingPillars.name: The off-market network
messagingPillars.description: Our most important inventory is never publicly listed. Membership in our private database is by introduction only.

messagingPillars.name: Cinematic presentation
messagingPillars.description: Every property is presented with editorial photography and film. We sell the life the home enables, not just its square footage.

donts: Avoid generic luxury cliches like 'dream home'

Modern.logoDirection: A finely-spaced sans-serif wordmark with an ampersand treated as a bespoke ligature mark. Generous letter-spacing signals confidence and air; the mark works embossed on stationery and as a minimal favicon.

typography.primary: Canela or a high-contrast modern serif for headlines
typography.secondary: Söhne or Neue Haas Grotesk for body
typography.rationale: A modern serif lends editorial gravitas while a clean grotesque keeps the system contemporary and legible across digital listing pages.

visualIdentityIdeas: Cinematic 16:9 property films with minimal lower-third typography
Embossed bone stationery with brass foil ampersand
An 'off-market' invitation card system in matte black
Map-coordinate motif referencing the meridian line
Editorial grid layouts that treat listings like magazine spreads

Modern.brandDescription: Keyrise is a tech-forward brokerage built specifically for first-time and starter-home buyers. It demystifies the process with transparent fee structures, salaried buyer-advisors, and a guided digital journey from pre-approval to closing. The brand treats the first purchase as a milestone to be coached, not a commission to be chased.
Modern.scope: A complete identity and product brand covering app UI brand layer, educational content system, agent co-branding kit, and social-first marketing. The work defines a friendly-but-credible voice and an explainer-driven content engine.
Modern.brandNameRationale: 'Key' is the universal symbol of homeownership and the literal handover at closing; 'rise' signals upward mobility and the rising generation of new owners. Together it reads as the moment of getting your first key.
Modern.industrySummary: In 2025 first-time buyers hit historic lows as a share of the market (around a quarter of buyers), squeezed by 6.5-7% mortgage rates, record-high median prices, and thin entry-level inventory. Down-payment assistance and rate buydowns became decisive levers, and the median first-time buyer age climbed to the late 30s. Builders increasingly courted this segment with smaller floor plans and incentive financing.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Redfin (redfin.com) attracts cost-conscious buyers with lower fees; Opendoor (opendoor.com) appeals to those wanting simplicity; Better (better.com) competes on digital mortgage speed. Keyrise differs by being a dedicated coaching brand for first purchases, bundling education, assistance-program matching, and salaried advisors with no incentive to upsell.
Modern.positioningStatement: For renters ready to buy their first home, Keyrise is the guided brokerage that turns an intimidating process into a clear, coached path.
Modern.positioningRationale: First-timers churn on confusion and fear, not affordability alone; a coaching brand with salaried advisors removes the trust deficit. Transparency and education are underserved in a commission-driven category, making it a credible differentiator.

targetAudience.primary: Renters aged 28-40, often dual-income millennials and older Gen Z, with stable jobs but limited home-buying knowledge and modest savings. They are digitally native, research-heavy, and skeptical of sales pressure. They start the journey online months before contacting an agent and expect transparency on every fee.
behaviors: Research affordability calculators and assistance programs online for months
Read reviews and Reddit threads before trusting an agent
Prefer texting and async chat over phone calls
Comparison-shop mortgage rates aggressively
motivations: Stop renting and build equity
Feel in control of a confusing process
Avoid being upsold beyond their budget

Modern.mission: To make the first home purchase clear, fair, and achievable for a generation priced out of confidence.
Modern.vision: To become the default starting point for everyone buying their first home.

messagingPillars.name: No jargon, ever
messagingPillars.description: We translate escrow, PMI, and points into plain language. If you don't understand it, we haven't explained it yet.

messagingPillars.name: Coached, not sold
messagingPillars.description: Our advisors are salaried, so their only job is getting you the right home. There's no incentive to push you higher.

messagingPillars.name: Money you didn't know you could get
messagingPillars.description: We match you with down-payment assistance and buydown programs. Most first-timers leave thousands on the table.

donts: Never use scarcity or pressure tactics

Modern.logoDirection: A geometric sans-serif wordmark with a key-tooth motif integrated into the letter 'k' or a rising-key icon. The mark should feel app-native, scalable to a 16px favicon, and warm rather than corporate.

typography.primary: Inter or Geist for UI and headlines
typography.secondary: Inter for body and educational content
typography.rationale: A single highly-legible geometric sans keeps the brand approachable and app-native, optimized for explainer content and small mobile type.

visualIdentityIdeas: Step-by-step progress bar motif as a recurring brand device

Modern.tagline: Space that works as hard as you do.
Modern.brandDescription: Tenant Axis is a commercial office leasing advisory representing occupiers in negotiating and structuring office space in a post-hybrid market. It combines workplace strategy, market analytics, and lease negotiation to align real estate with how teams actually work. The firm is data-led and tenant-aligned, never representing landlords.
Modern.scope: A B2B brand system spanning wordmark, pitch decks, market-report templates, and a data-dashboard brand layer. The engagement defines an analytical, consultative voice for C-suite and HR/workplace audiences.
Modern.brandNameRationale: 'Tenant' signals exclusive occupier representation and whose side the firm is on; 'Axis' implies the strategic pivot point around which a workplace decision turns. Together it reads as the tenant's center of gravity.
Modern.industrySummary: Office leasing in 2025 remains bifurcated: national office vacancy sits near record highs (around 19-20%) as hybrid work persists, yet a clear flight-to-quality concentrates demand in trophy and amenity-rich Class A buildings. Tenants hold negotiating leverage, securing concessions, shorter terms, and flexible footprints, while distressed Class B/C assets struggle. Right-sizing and 'less space, better space' define occupier strategy.
Modern.competitorLandscape: CBRE (cbre.com) and JLL (jll.com) dominate with full-service scale but often represent both sides; Savills (savills.us) emphasizes tenant-only representation. Tenant Axis differs by being purely occupier-aligned, lean, and analytics-forward, pairing every lease with a workplace-utilization study.
Modern.positioningStatement: For occupiers rethinking the office, Tenant Axis is the tenant-only advisor that turns workplace strategy into the right lease.
Modern.positioningRationale: Conflict-free representation matters most when landlords hold weaker hands and concessions are negotiable; a tenant-only stance builds trust. Pairing data with workplace strategy meets the central 2025 question of how much and what kind of space a company truly needs.

targetAudience.primary: Heads of real estate, CFOs, and workplace/HR leaders at companies with 50-2,000 employees facing lease renewals or relocations. They are analytical, cost-conscious, and navigating hybrid-work uncertainty. They want data to defend decisions to their board and fear committing to the wrong footprint for a decade.
behaviors: Commission utilization and headcount-projection studies before renewing
Benchmark concessions and TI allowances against market comps
Involve finance and HR jointly in space decisions
Favor flexibility and shorter terms over long commitments
motivations: Avoid over-committing to space in an uncertain hybrid era
Defend real estate decisions with data
Negotiate maximum concessions

Modern.mission: To align every office lease with how a company actually works, on terms that favor the tenant.
Modern.vision: To make conflict-free, data-led occupier advisory the standard for office leasing.

messagingPillars.name: Always the tenant's side
messagingPillars.description: We never represent landlords, so there's no conflict in the room. Our leverage is your leverage.

messagingPillars.name: Space follows strategy
messagingPillars.description: We study how your teams work before we tour a single floor. The lease should serve the workplace, not the other way around.

messagingPillars.name: Concessions are negotiable
messagingPillars.description: In today's market, free rent, TI dollars, and flexibility are on the table. We benchmark every term against live comps.

Modern.logoDirection: A precise grotesque wordmark with an axis/crosshair glyph formed from intersecting lines. The mark should feel like a data instrument: structured, gridded, and confident in monochrome.

typography.primary: Neue Haas Grotesk or Suisse Int'l for headlines
typography.secondary: IBM Plex Sans for body and data tables
typography.rationale: A Swiss grotesque conveys analytical precision while Plex's tabular figures make market reports and lease comparisons read cleanly.

visualIdentityIdeas: Crosshair/axis motif marking the 'right space' on a market map
Concession benchmark bar charts as hero graphics
Side-by-side lease-term comparison tables as a signature layout

Modern.tagline: Where foot traffic meets the right tenant.
Modern.brandDescription: Frontage Co. is a retail and storefront leasing brokerage matching consumer brands with high-performing physical locations. It blends location analytics, trade-area data, and merchandising insight to place tenants where their customers already walk. The firm advises both expanding retailers and landlords curating tenant mix.
Modern.scope: A brand identity for a retail-focused brokerage including wordmark, trade-area report templates, leasing flyers, and a deal-pipeline web presence. The work defines a voice fluent in both retail strategy and real estate.
Modern.brandNameRationale: 'Frontage' is the precise real estate term for a property's street-facing dimension, the very thing that drives retail visibility and value. It signals deep category fluency in storefront leasing.
Modern.industrySummary: Retail real estate in 2025 is the surprise strength of commercial property: vacancy sits near historic lows (around 4-5%) because almost no new retail has been built in over a decade. Limited supply gives landlords pricing power even as e-commerce reshapes formats toward experiential, service, and necessity-based tenants. Open-air and grocery-anchored centers outperform enclosed malls, and brands pursue selective omnichannel store expansion.
Modern.competitorLandscape: JLL Retail (jll.com) and CBRE Retail (cbre.com) bring national scale; SRS Real Estate Partners (srsre.com) is a retail-only specialist. Frontage Co. differs by combining trade-area data science with merchandising fluency, positioning itself as a retail strategist that happens to do leasing, for emerging and mid-market brands the giants overlook.
Modern.positioningStatement: For brands choosing where to plant a store, Frontage Co. is the retail leasing partner that reads foot traffic like a data scientist and merchandising like a buyer.
Modern.positioningRationale: Site selection failure is the top killer of retail expansion; pairing trade-area analytics with merchandising insight de-risks the decision. Mid-market and DTC brands going physical are underserved by enterprise brokerages, creating a clear niche.

targetAudience.primary: Real estate and expansion directors at growing retail and F&B brands (10-200 locations), plus DTC brands opening their first physical stores. They are metrics-driven, brand-protective, and wary of bad locations sinking unit economics. They evaluate sites on co-tenancy, demographics, and daypart traffic, and move fast when the right corner appears.
behaviors: Analyze trade-area demographics and daytime population before signing
Scrutinize co-tenancy and neighboring brands
Model unit economics per location obsessively
Expand in clusters to build regional density
motivations: Place stores where their exact customer already shops
Protect brand equity through the right neighbors
Hit unit-economics targets per location

Modern.mission: To place every brand in the location where its customers already are.
Modern.vision: To be the most data-fluent retail leasing partner for the brands defining the next era of physical retail.

messagingPillars.name: Read the street
messagingPillars.description: We analyze foot traffic, daypart, and trade-area demographics block by block. The right corner is a measurable thing.

messagingPillars.name: Co-tenancy is strategy
messagingPillars.description: Who you sit next to shapes who walks in. We curate neighbors as carefully as the address itself.

messagingPillars.name: Built for the omnichannel era
messagingPillars.description: Physical stores now serve fulfillment, brand, and discovery. We site stores for what retail has become, not what it was.

dos: Talk in foot-traffic and trade-area terms
Speak retail and real estate fluently

Modern.logoDirection: A bold, slightly condensed grotesque wordmark evoking a storefront sign, with an awning or threshold glyph. The mark should feel like signage itself, confident at large scale on a window decal.

typography.primary: Druk or a condensed grotesque for signage-style headlines
typography.secondary: Founders Grotesk or Inter for body
typography.rationale: A condensed display face mimics retail signage and grabs attention, while a clean grotesque keeps reports and data legible.

visualIdentityIdeas: Trade-area heat-map graphics as hero imagery
Street-level photography of storefronts with annotated frontage

Modern.tagline: The space behind the supply chain.
Modern.brandDescription: Throughline Industrial is a brokerage and advisory focused on warehouse, distribution, and logistics real estate. It serves 3PLs, manufacturers, and e-commerce operators needing space optimized for throughput, dock ratios, and clear height. The firm thinks in supply-chain terms, not just square feet.
Modern.scope: A B2B industrial brand system including wordmark, site-spec sheets, logistics market reports, and a property-search portal brand layer. The engagement defines an operationally fluent, infrastructure-grade voice.
Modern.brandNameRationale: 'Throughline' captures both the logistics flow through a facility and the connecting thread across a supply chain. 'Industrial' anchors the asset class plainly and credibly.
Modern.industrySummary: Industrial real estate in 2025 is normalizing after a pandemic-era boom: a wave of new construction pushed vacancy up to the 6-7% range, easing the historic tightness, yet rents for modern, well-located logistics space remain elevated. Nearshoring, e-commerce fulfillment, and inventory restocking sustain demand, with occupiers prizing high clear heights, ample trailer parking, and last-mile proximity. Big-box absorption cooled while small-bay and infill remain tight.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Prologis (prologis.com) is the dominant logistics REIT and developer; CBRE (cbre.com) and Cushman & Wakefield (cushmanwakefield.com) lead industrial brokerage. Throughline differs by being a specialist advisory that reads facilities through a supply-chain-engineering lens, serving mid-market 3PLs and manufacturers rather than only mega-box occupiers.
Modern.positioningStatement: For operators who move goods, Throughline Industrial is the brokerage that selects space by throughput, not just rate.
Modern.positioningRationale: Logistics performance lives or dies on dock ratios, clear height, and location-to-network fit, which generalist brokers underweight; a throughput-first lens is a real differentiator. Mid-market operators need this rigor but lack enterprise real estate teams.

targetAudience.primary: Supply-chain, operations, and real estate leaders at 3PLs, manufacturers, and e-commerce companies needing 50,000-500,000 sq ft. They are operationally minded, ROI-driven, and obsessive about location relative to ports, highways, and population. They evaluate dock doors, trailer parking, power, and clear height as seriously as rent.
behaviors: Spec facilities by dock ratio, clear height, and trailer stalls
Map sites against transportation networks and labor pools
Model occupancy cost against logistics throughput
Plan for automation and racking density upfront
motivations: Maximize throughput and minimize transport cost
Secure scarce modern logistics space
Future-proof facilities for automation

Modern.mission: To match logistics operators with facilities engineered for how goods actually flow.
Modern.vision: To be the specialist advisor of record for the modern supply chain's real estate.

messagingPillars.name: Specs that matter
messagingPillars.description: Clear height, dock ratio, power, and trailer parking decide a facility's value to you. We lead with the specs that drive throughput.

messagingPillars.name: Location is a network
messagingPillars.description: A building is only as good as its position relative to ports, highways, and labor. We map sites against your whole network.

messagingPillars.name: Built for what's next
messagingPillars.description: Automation, racking density, and EV fleets are reshaping facilities. We advise for the next ten years, not the last lease.

dos: Tie real estate to logistics cost

typography.primary: Roboto Condensed or DIN Next for headlines
typography.secondary: IBM Plex Sans for body and spec sheets
typography.rationale: A DIN-style engineered face evokes industrial signage and standards, while Plex keeps dense spec tables clean and tabular.

Annotated facility cutaways showing clear height and docks

Modern.tagline: Owned by you. Run by us.
Modern.brandDescription: Tenant & Keep is a residential property management company handling leasing, maintenance, rent collection, and tenant relations for single-family and small multifamily owners. It pairs responsive on-the-ground service with an owner dashboard that makes performance transparent. The brand is built for accidental and intentional landlords who want hands-off ownership.
Modern.scope: A brand system for a property-management firm covering wordmark, owner and tenant portal brand layers, onboarding collateral, and maintenance-team identity. The work defines a reliable, transparent voice for two audiences: owners and renters.
Modern.brandNameRationale: 'Tenant' centers the resident relationship that drives retention, while 'Keep' evokes both upkeep and the safekeeping of an owner's asset. Together it reads as caretaking from both sides.
Modern.industrySummary: Residential property management in 2025 rides a strong renter market: elevated mortgage rates kept would-be buyers renting longer, sustaining high occupancy and steady rent growth in single-family rentals. Institutional SFR ownership expanded, but mom-and-pop owners still hold the majority of units and increasingly outsource management amid tighter regulation and maintenance-cost inflation. Tenant expectations for digital payments, fast maintenance, and self-service portals are now table stakes.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Mynd (mynd.co) and Evernest (evernest.co) scale tech-enabled SFR management; local franchises like Real Property Management (realpropertymgt.com) blanket markets. Tenant & Keep differs by combining hyper-responsive maintenance SLAs with radical owner transparency, positioning service quality over pure scale.
Modern.positioningStatement: For owners who want income without the headaches, Tenant & Keep is the property manager that treats your asset like its own and your tenants like guests.
Modern.positioningRationale: Owners churn managers over poor communication and surprise costs; transparency plus maintenance SLAs directly target those pain points. Treating tenants well drives retention, which is the single biggest lever on owner returns, aligning both audiences.

targetAudience.primary: Individual and small-portfolio rental owners (1-20 units), including accidental landlords and out-of-state investors, plus their tenants. Owners are busy professionals who want passive income without 2am maintenance calls and distrust opaque managers. Tenants are renters who expect digital payments, quick repairs, and respectful communication.
behaviors: Owners review monthly statements and want real-time visibility
Owners hire after a bad self-management or prior-manager experience
Tenants pay rent and submit maintenance requests via app
Tenants weigh renewal on responsiveness and respect
motivations: Owners want truly hands-off, transparent income
Owners want to protect and grow asset value
Tenants want responsive, respectful management

Modern.mission: To make rental ownership effortless for owners and renting a pleasure for tenants.
Modern.vision: To set the standard for transparent, responsive residential property management.

messagingPillars.name: You always know
messagingPillars.description: Your owner dashboard shows income, expenses, and maintenance in real time. No surprises, no chasing for statements.

messagingPillars.name: Fast on the small stuff
messagingPillars.description: We answer maintenance requests within hours, not days. Quick fixes keep tenants happy and assets sound.

messagingPillars.name: Happy tenants stay
messagingPillars.description: We treat residents with respect because retention is your best return. Every renewal saves a turnover.

dos: Speak to both owners and tenants respectfully

Modern.logoDirection: A clean humanist sans wordmark with an ampersand and a subtle roofline or key-fob glyph. The mark should feel trustworthy and contemporary, working as an app icon and a yard sign alike.

typography.primary: Aeonik or General Sans for headlines
typography.secondary: Inter for body and portal UI
typography.rationale: A friendly geometric sans signals modernity and trust, while Inter ensures portal data and statements stay legible on every device.

visualIdentityIdeas: Roofline icon system for property types
Calm photography of homes and friendly maintenance teams

Modern.brandDescription: Commonhold Operations is a commercial property management firm running office, retail, and mixed-use assets on behalf of institutional and private owners. It handles operations, tenant relations, capital projects, and ESG performance with a technology-enabled, data-reported approach. The brand is positioned as an operating partner that protects asset value and NOI.
Modern.scope: A B2B brand system including wordmark, owner reporting templates, tenant-experience touchpoints, building signage standards, and an operations-dashboard brand layer. The work defines an institutional, performance-oriented voice.
Modern.brandNameRationale: 'Commonhold' references shared building ownership and the common areas a manager stewards; 'Operations' states the discipline plainly. Together it conveys rigorous stewardship of shared commercial assets.
Modern.industrySummary: Commercial property management in 2025 is defined by operational scrutiny: with office values reset and NOI under pressure, owners demand managers who can cut operating costs, retain tenants, and deliver granular reporting. ESG and building-decarbonization mandates (energy benchmarking, local laws like NYC's emissions caps) raised the bar on technical management. Tenant-experience amenities and flexible terms became retention tools as occupancy stabilized below pre-2020 levels.
Modern.competitorLandscape: CBRE (cbre.com) and JLL (jll.com) offer integrated property management at global scale; Cushman & Wakefield (cushmanwakefield.com) competes across asset classes. Commonhold Operations differs as a focused operating partner emphasizing NOI optimization, ESG compliance, and transparent reporting for mid-market and private institutional owners underserved by the giants.
Modern.positioningStatement: For owners protecting asset value, Commonhold Operations is the management partner that runs buildings for NOI, compliance, and retention.
Modern.positioningRationale: In a reset market, operational excellence and cost discipline directly defend valuations, making NOI-focused management compelling. ESG and emissions compliance are now operational risks, and a manager fluent in both is differentiated from generalists.

targetAudience.primary: Asset managers, private owners, and institutional investors holding commercial buildings who need operational performance and reporting they can trust. They are financially rigorous, compliance-aware, and value-protection focused. They scrutinize operating budgets, capital plans, and tenant retention metrics and expect institutional-grade reporting.
behaviors: Review monthly NOI and operating-expense variance reports
Demand ESG and energy-benchmarking compliance
Prioritize tenant retention to protect occupancy
Approve capital plans tied to value preservation
motivations: Protect and grow asset value and NOI
Stay compliant with emissions and ESG mandates
Retain tenants and stabilize occupancy

Modern.mission: To operate commercial buildings with the rigor that protects their value and the service that retains their tenants.
Modern.vision: To be the operating partner of choice for owners who measure management in NOI and compliance.

messagingPillars.name: Managed for NOI
messagingPillars.description: Every operating decision is measured against net operating income. We cut waste without cutting tenant experience.

messagingPillars.name: Compliance is operations
messagingPillars.description: Energy benchmarking and emissions caps are now core to running a building. We keep your assets ahead of the mandates.

messagingPillars.name: Retention is value
messagingPillars.description: Keeping tenants in place protects occupancy and valuation. We treat tenant experience as an asset-management lever.

dos: Speak in NOI and operating metrics
donts: Avoid consumer warmth in B2B reporting

Modern.logoDirection: A structured grotesque wordmark paired with a building-grid or modular block glyph. The mark should feel institutional and systematic, equally at home on a lobby plaque and a reporting cover page.

typography.primary: Suisse Int'l or Neue Montreal for headlines
typography.secondary: IBM Plex Sans for reporting and body
typography.rationale: A precise neutral grotesque conveys institutional credibility, while Plex's tabular figures serve dense operating reports.

visualIdentityIdeas: Building-grid motif representing portfolio and common areas
NOI and OpEx variance dashboard graphics
Lobby signage and wayfinding standards mockups

Modern.brandDescription: Infill & Co. is an urban infill developer building thoughtfully-scaled residential and mixed-use projects on overlooked lots within established city neighborhoods. It specializes in entitlement-complex sites, adaptive reuse, and missing-middle housing. The brand champions walkable density that strengthens, rather than disrupts, existing communities.
Modern.scope: A development brand covering wordmark, project naming framework, community-engagement collateral, leasing/sales identity, and a hoarding/signage system. The work defines a civic, design-literate voice for residents, city stakeholders, and capital partners.
Modern.brandNameRationale: 'Infill' is the precise planning term for developing vacant or underused parcels within existing urban fabric. It directly names the firm's discipline and signals a pro-density, anti-sprawl ethos.
Modern.industrySummary: Urban infill in 2025 benefits from a national policy tailwind: zoning reforms legalizing ADUs, duplexes, and 'missing middle' housing spread across cities, while high land and construction costs make efficient small-lot development attractive. Demand for walkable, transit-adjacent living remains strong among younger households, even as elevated interest rates and lengthy entitlements pressure project feasibility. Adaptive reuse of obsolete commercial buildings gained momentum amid the office glut.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Trammell Crow Residential (trammellcrow.com) and Toll Brothers' City Living (tollbrothers.com) pursue urban density at scale; Jonathan Rose Companies (rosecompanies.com) emphasizes green, community-minded infill. Infill & Co. differs by focusing on small-to-mid complex sites and missing-middle typologies, with deep community-engagement and design quality the big players skip.
Modern.positioningStatement: For neighborhoods that deserve growth without losing their character, Infill & Co. is the developer building human-scaled density that fits.
Modern.positioningRationale: Community opposition kills infill projects; a brand built on engagement and contextual design de-risks entitlement and earns local support. Missing-middle typologies are an underbuilt, policy-favored niche large developers ignore, creating a defensible focus.

targetAudience.primary: Two audiences: urban renters/buyers aged 28-45 seeking walkable, well-designed homes; and city planners, neighbors, and capital partners who must approve and fund projects. Residents value design, location, and community; stakeholders value contextual fit and credibility. Both reward developers who listen and build quality over those who maximize and extract.
behaviors: Residents prioritize walkability and transit access
Neighbors scrutinize scale, parking, and design at hearings
Capital partners assess entitlement risk and design pro-forma
Buyers value architectural quality over raw square footage
motivations: Residents want walkable, design-forward urban living
Communities want growth that respects character
Partners want de-risked, well-designed projects

Modern.mission: To build walkable, well-designed homes on the overlooked lots that make cities better.
Modern.vision: To prove that thoughtful density is the most valuable kind of growth.

messagingPillars.name: Built to fit
messagingPillars.description: We design to the scale and texture of the block, not against it. Good infill makes a neighborhood feel more itself.

messagingPillars.name: The missing middle
messagingPillars.description: Duplexes, courtyards, and small apartments are the housing cities forgot how to build. We specialize in the typologies between the house and the tower.

messagingPillars.name: We start by listening
messagingPillars.description: Community input shapes our projects before the first rendering. Engagement isn't a hurdle, it's how good places get made.

Modern.logoDirection: A clean architectural sans wordmark with an ampersand and a tessellating block/lot glyph suggesting parcels fitting together. The mark should feel like a thoughtful site plan, modern and modular.

typography.primary: GT America or Neue Haas Grotesk for headlines
typography.secondary: Inter for body
typography.rationale: An architectural grotesque conveys design credibility while staying civic and approachable across hearing decks and marketing.

visualIdentityIdeas: Site-plan line drawings as decorative motif

Modern.brandDescription: Wayfield Communities develops large master-planned communities integrating homes, schools, retail, parks, and trails into cohesive new neighborhoods. It orchestrates land planning, builder partnerships, and amenity programming over multi-year horizons. The brand sells not just homes but a designed way of life with built-in connection.
Modern.scope: A master-brand and place-brand system covering community naming, wayfinding and signage, amenity identity, model-home sales-center experience, and a lifestyle marketing platform. The work defines an aspirational yet grounded voice across a decade-long buildout.
Modern.brandNameRationale: 'Wayfield' fuses 'way' (paths, trails, ways of living) with 'field' (the land being developed), evoking open, connected places. It suggests a planned landscape designed for everyday life.
Modern.industrySummary: Master-planned communities in 2025 remain a resilient bright spot in homebuilding: the top MPCs continued to lead new-home sales as buyers sought affordability, amenities, and community in Sun Belt growth markets like Texas, Florida, Arizona, and the Carolinas. Builders leaned on mortgage-rate buydowns to keep these communities moving despite 6.5-7% rates. Demand skewed toward amenity-rich, trail-connected, multi-generational communities with built-in lifestyle.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Howard Hughes (howardhughes.com) develops large-scale MPCs like Summerlin and The Woodlands; Brookfield Residential (brookfieldresidential.com) and Hines (hines.com) build amenity-rich communities nationally. Wayfield differs by emphasizing connection and walkable, trail-linked design over sheer scale, programming community life as deliberately as it plans roads.
Modern.positioningStatement: For families choosing where to put down roots, Wayfield Communities builds neighborhoods designed for connection, not just construction.
Modern.positioningRationale: Buyers in MPCs are buying belonging and lifestyle as much as a house; programming connection differentiates from amenity checklists. Walkable, trail-linked design meets a clear demand and is harder to replicate than pools and clubhouses alone.

targetAudience.primary: Move-up families and relocating households aged 30-55 plus active empty-nesters, buying in growth-market suburbs. They value schools, safety, amenities, and a sense of community, and are willing to pay a premium for lifestyle and convenience. They research communities extensively, visit on weekends, and decide based on the feel of the place and its future plan.
behaviors: Tour multiple communities and amenity centers before deciding
Research school ratings and future-phase plans
Value trails, parks, and events as much as the home itself
Engage with community social calendars and HOA programming
motivations: Give their family a connected, safe community
Access amenities and lifestyle without leaving the neighborhood
Invest in a place with a planned, appreciating future

Modern.mission: To plan and build communities where connection, nature, and convenience are designed in from day one.
Modern.vision: To create the most loved master-planned communities in America's fastest-growing regions.

messagingPillars.name: Connection by design
messagingPillars.description: Trails, gathering spaces, and events are planned to bring neighbors together. We program community life, not just lay out lots.

messagingPillars.name: A plan you can trust
messagingPillars.description: Schools, parks, and retail are mapped from the start across every phase. Buyers can see the future of where they're investing.

messagingPillars.name: Nature in the everyday
messagingPillars.description: Greenways and open space weave through the community. Daily life happens steps from the outdoors.

Modern.logoDirection: An open, friendly geometric sans wordmark with a path/trail or contour-line glyph weaving through it. The mark should feel expansive and welcoming, scaling from monument signage to a community app.

typography.primary: Sofia or Gilroy for headlines
typography.secondary: Inter for body
typography.rationale: A rounded geometric sans feels welcoming and contemporary, suited to lifestyle marketing and clear community wayfinding.

visualIdentityIdeas: Contour-line and trail motif across signage
Illustrated community master-map as a hero asset
Lifestyle photography of families on trails and at events
Phase-plan timeline showing the community's future

Modern.brandDescription: Plotline is a consumer real estate search portal that aggregates listings with transparent data, neighborhood intelligence, and AI-assisted search. It surfaces the facts buyers actually need, price history, true days-on-market, school and commute data, in a clean interface free of pay-to-play clutter. The brand competes on trust and data clarity.
Modern.scope: A digital-product brand including app and web UI brand layer, search-experience design language, data-visualization system, and a content/SEO identity. The work defines a clear, data-literate, trustworthy voice.
Modern.brandNameRationale: 'Plotline' merges 'plot' (a parcel of land) with the narrative thread of a property's story, its price history and neighborhood context. It signals a portal that tells the full, honest story of every listing.
Modern.industrySummary: PropTech search portals in 2025 are reshaping discovery amid the post-NAR-settlement transparency push: buyer-agent commission changes and demand for clear data put pressure on legacy portals' pay-to-play lead models. Consumers want accurate days-on-market, price history, and total cost of ownership, not inflated 'Zestimate'-style guesses. AI-assisted natural-language search and richer neighborhood data became key differentiators as listing accuracy and trust rose in importance.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Zillow (zillow.com) leads on traffic but is criticized for estimates and agent ads; Redfin (redfin.com) pairs portal with brokerage; Realtor.com (realtor.com) emphasizes listing accuracy. Plotline differs by being agnostic and ad-light, prioritizing transparent data and AI search over lead monetization, positioning trust as the product.
Modern.positioningStatement: For buyers tired of guesswork, Plotline is the search portal that shows the real story behind every listing.
Modern.positioningRationale: Trust is the unmet need legacy portals created with inflated estimates and pay-to-play results; a transparency-first portal is genuinely differentiated. AI-assisted search and honest data align with what post-settlement, data-hungry buyers now expect.

targetAudience.primary: Active home searchers aged 28-55 across buying and renting, who are digitally fluent and research-obsessed. They browse listings nightly, distrust inflated estimates, and want commute, school, and price-history data in one place. They are skeptical of being funneled to paying agents and reward platforms that feel honest and uncluttered.
behaviors: Browse listings nightly across multiple apps
Cross-check price history and days-on-market for accuracy
Set granular saved-search alerts
Distrust automated home-value estimates
motivations: See the real, unspun data on every property
Search naturally without ad clutter
Avoid being funneled to pay-to-play agents

Modern.mission: To make every property's true story visible to the people deciding on it.
Modern.vision: To become the most trusted place to search for a home.

messagingPillars.name: The whole story
messagingPillars.description: Price history, true days-on-market, and neighborhood data, all in one place. We don't hide the parts that matter.

messagingPillars.name: Search like you talk
messagingPillars.description: Ask for 'a 3-bed near good schools under 20 minutes from downtown' and get it. AI search understands what you actually want.

messagingPillars.name: No pay-to-play
messagingPillars.description: Results aren't sold to the highest-bidding agent. What you see is the market, not an ad auction.

Modern.logoDirection: A precise, modern geometric sans wordmark with a subtle plotted-line or pin glyph integrated into a letter. The mark should feel like a clean data product: minimal, confident, and crisp at favicon scale.

typography.secondary: Geist Mono for data and numbers
typography.rationale: A modern neutral sans keeps the product clean and tech-forward, while a mono companion lends data and price figures a precise, trustworthy feel.

visualIdentityIdeas: Price-history line charts as a signature data viz
Natural-language search bar as hero device
Clean listing-card design language with honest data badges

Modern.tagline: Sell on your terms. Skip the wait.
Modern.brandDescription: Settled is an instant-offer (iBuyer) platform that makes competitive cash offers on homes and lets sellers choose their close date. It removes the uncertainty of listings, showings, and contingent buyers with a transparent, fee-clear process. The brand emphasizes certainty and control for sellers who value speed over squeezing the last dollar.
Modern.scope: A consumer fintech-meets-real-estate brand covering wordmark, offer-flow UI brand layer, trust-and-transparency collateral, and performance-marketing identity. The work defines a calm, certainty-driven, transparent voice.
Modern.brandNameRationale: 'Settled' evokes both the closing/settlement of a real estate transaction and the emotional relief of a done deal. It promises the calm certainty the iBuyer model exists to deliver.
Modern.industrySummary: The iBuyer category in 2025 is leaner and more disciplined after the 2022-23 shakeout that ended Zillow Offers and Redfin's iBuying: Opendoor and Offerpad survived by tightening pricing models amid rate volatility and thinner margins. Higher rates and choppy home prices make algorithmic pricing riskier, so survivors emphasize transparency and partner-agent models. Sellers value certainty and speed in a market where traditional sales can stall on financing fall-throughs.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Opendoor (opendoor.com) is the category leader by volume; Offerpad (offerpad.com) competes with flexible close dates and renovation services; Zillow (zillow.com) now refers sellers rather than buying directly. Settled differs by leading with radical fee transparency and seller-choice on timing, avoiding the opaque-deduction reputation that dogged early iBuyers.
Modern.positioningStatement: For sellers who value certainty over chance, Settled is the instant-offer platform that pays cash on your timeline with no surprises.
Modern.positioningRationale: Distrust of hidden fees and lowball offers is the iBuyer category's central liability; leading with transparency directly neutralizes it. Certainty and date-flexibility address the real anxiety, a sale falling through, that motivates iBuyer sellers.

targetAudience.primary: Homeowners aged 35-65 needing to sell quickly or with certainty, including relocators, divorcing couples, estate sellers, and move-up buyers who can't carry two mortgages. They value convenience and predictability over maximum price, and are anxious about showings, financing fall-throughs, and timing two transactions. They research the trade-off carefully and want every fee disclosed upfront.
behaviors: Compare instant offers against estimated agent-sale net
Prioritize close-date certainty over top dollar
Scrutinize fees and deductions before accepting
Sell under time pressure (relocation, life change)
motivations: Sell with certainty and avoid fall-throughs
Control the timing around a move or life event
Skip showings and the uncertainty of listing

Modern.mission: To give every seller a certain, transparent way to sell on their own timeline.
Modern.vision: To make the instant, certain home sale a trusted mainstream option.

messagingPillars.name: Certainty, not chance
messagingPillars.description: A real cash offer means no showings, no financing fall-throughs, no maybe. You know the number and the date.

messagingPillars.name: Every fee, upfront
messagingPillars.description: We show our offer and our fees side by side before you decide. No surprise deductions at closing.

messagingPillars.name: Your timeline, your call
messagingPillars.description: Close in two weeks or two months, you choose. The sale fits your move, not ours.

Modern.logoDirection: A confident, rounded geometric sans wordmark conveying ease and finality, perhaps with a subtle checkmark or settled-line baseline. The mark should feel fintech-clean and reassuring at app and billboard scale.

typography.primary: Aeonik or Circular for headlines
typography.secondary: Inter for UI and body
typography.rationale: A friendly geometric sans signals fintech ease and reassurance, while Inter keeps offer details and fee breakdowns precise and legible.

visualIdentityIdeas: Close-date selector as a signature UI motif

Modern.brandDescription: Roomscale is a 3D tour and virtual staging platform that turns property scans into immersive, shoppable digital tours and AI-staged interiors. It serves agents, brokerages, and builders who want listings to sell faster with photoreal virtual furnishing and accurate spatial data. The brand sits at the intersection of spatial computing and real estate marketing.
Modern.scope: A SaaS brand covering wordmark, product UI brand layer, capture-app identity, demo/onboarding collateral, and a developer/API brand. The work defines a technical-yet-creative voice for real estate professionals.
Modern.brandNameRationale: 'Roomscale' borrows the spatial-computing term for movement through a real-size virtual space, signaling immersive, true-to-scale tours. It conveys both the room (the listing) and the scale (accurate dimensions) the product delivers.
Modern.industrySummary: Virtual staging and 3D tours in 2025 ride two waves: generative AI slashed virtual-staging costs and turnaround to near-instant, while buyers increasingly expect immersive tours after pandemic-era habits stuck. With inventory tight and listings competitive, agents use 3D tours and AI staging to reduce days-on-market and pre-qualify remote buyers. Matterport's acquisition by CoStar and a flood of AI-staging startups intensified the space, raising the bar on photorealism and ease.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Matterport (matterport.com) leads 3D capture and digital twins; Zillow 3D Home (zillow.com) offers free agent tours; BoxBrownie (boxbrownie.com) and virtual-staging AI tools handle photoreal staging. Roomscale differs by unifying accurate 3D capture with instant AI staging in one workflow, targeting speed and photorealism for everyday agents, not just enterprise.
Modern.positioningStatement: For agents who need listings to stand out, Roomscale turns a phone scan into an immersive, fully-staged tour in minutes.
Modern.positioningRationale: Agents want one tool that does capture and staging without separate vendors or delays; unifying the workflow is a clear gap. Speed and photorealism are the exact levers that cut days-on-market, tying the product directly to the agent's economic goal.

targetAudience.primary: Real estate agents, listing coordinators, and builder marketing teams who produce listing media regularly. They are tech-adopting but time-poor, judged on days-on-market, and cost-conscious about marketing spend. They want professional results without hiring photographers and stagers for every listing, and they value speed and ease above all.
behaviors: Capture listings on their phone between showings
Compare days-on-market with and without 3D tours
Reuse listing media across MLS, social, and email
Adopt tools that promise faster, cheaper marketing
motivations: Reduce days-on-market with standout listings
Cut staging and photography costs
Serve remote and out-of-state buyers

Modern.mission: To make immersive, beautifully-staged property tours instant and accessible to every agent.
Modern.vision: To make the 3D, staged tour the default way the world experiences real estate online.

messagingPillars.name: Scan to staged in minutes
messagingPillars.description: Capture with your phone and let AI furnish empty rooms instantly. What took days and a stager now takes a coffee break.

messagingPillars.name: True to scale
messagingPillars.description: Every tour preserves accurate dimensions and floor plans. Buyers explore the real space, not a flattering illusion.

messagingPillars.name: Sell to anyone, anywhere
messagingPillars.description: Immersive tours pre-qualify remote and relocating buyers before they ever visit. Your listing works around the clock.

Modern.logoDirection: A modern geometric sans wordmark with a cubic/isometric room glyph suggesting 3D space. The mark should feel like spatial software: dimensional, clean, and animatable for product demos.

typography.primary: Space Grotesk or Geist for headlines
typography.secondary: Inter for body and UI
typography.rationale: A geometric display sans with technical character suits a spatial-computing product, while Inter keeps the product UI clean and legible.

Modern.brandDescription: Cornerstone Yield Trust is a diversified real estate investment trust offering investors income and growth through a curated portfolio of income-producing properties. It emphasizes disciplined capital allocation, durable cash flow, and transparent investor reporting. The brand speaks to both institutional allocators and sophisticated retail investors seeking real-asset income.
Modern.scope: An investor-grade brand system covering wordmark, investor-relations identity, quarterly-report and earnings-deck templates, fact-sheet design, and an IR website brand layer. The work defines a credible, financially-literate, transparent voice.
Modern.brandNameRationale: 'Cornerstone' signals foundational stability and the literal building block of real estate; 'Yield Trust' names the product, income from a trust, with plain credibility. Together it conveys a dependable, income-anchored vehicle.
Modern.industrySummary: REITs in 2025 navigate a pivotal rate environment: after a brutal 2022-23 repricing, the prospect of Fed rate cuts improved sentiment, narrowing the gap between public REIT valuations and private real estate. Sector dispersion is extreme, data centers, industrial, and senior housing thrive while office REITs remain pressured. Investors prize REITs with strong balance sheets, well-covered dividends, and exposure to secular-demand property types over leveraged, rate-sensitive names.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Realty Income (realtyincome.com) is the dividend-focused 'Monthly Dividend Company'; Prologis (prologis.com) leads logistics REITs; Blackstone's BREIT (breit.com) dominates non-traded retail REITs. Cornerstone Yield Trust differs by emphasizing diversified, secular-demand property exposure with radical reporting transparency, targeting investors burned by opaque non-traded vehicles.
Modern.positioningStatement: For investors who want real-asset income they can trust, Cornerstone Yield Trust delivers durable yield with disciplined allocation and full transparency.
Modern.positioningRationale: Post-repricing, investors reward balance-sheet strength and well-covered dividends; leading with discipline and transparency builds credibility. Skepticism toward opaque non-traded REITs creates an opening for a transparency-first brand.

targetAudience.primary: Institutional allocators, RIAs, and sophisticated retail investors seeking real-asset income and portfolio diversification. They are financially literate, risk-aware, and yield-focused, scrutinizing dividend coverage, leverage, and FFO growth. They demand transparent reporting and are wary of vehicles with hidden fees or illiquidity after the non-traded REIT scrutiny of recent years.
behaviors: Analyze FFO, dividend coverage, and debt maturities before investing
Compare yield against risk and property-type exposure
Read quarterly reports and earnings calls closely
Favor liquidity and transparency over opaque structures
motivations: Earn durable, real-asset income
Diversify portfolios with hard assets
Trust the manager's discipline and disclosure

Modern.mission: To deliver durable real-asset income through disciplined allocation and uncommon transparency.
Modern.vision: To be the most trusted name in income-focused real estate investing.

messagingPillars.name: Yield with discipline
messagingPillars.description: We allocate capital to durable, well-covered income, not chase headline returns. Sustainable yield beats fleeting yield.

messagingPillars.name: Built on real ground
messagingPillars.description: Our income comes from tangible, income-producing properties in secular-demand sectors. Hard assets anchor the portfolio.

messagingPillars.name: Nothing hidden
messagingPillars.description: We report leverage, coverage, and fees in plain terms every quarter. Investors deserve to see exactly what they own.

dos: Speak in FFO, coverage, and allocation terms

Modern.logoDirection: A solid, refined grotesque or transitional-serif wordmark with a cornerstone/keystone block glyph. The mark should feel institutional and trustworthy, equally credible on an annual report and a stock ticker page.

typography.primary: Tiempos or a transitional serif for headlines
typography.secondary: Söhne or Inter for body and data
typography.rationale: A transitional serif lends institutional gravitas to investor materials, while a clean grotesque keeps financial tables and fact sheets precise.

visualIdentityIdeas: Map of portfolio holdings by sector

Modern.brandDescription: Vesta Living is a multifamily apartment operator managing and lease-marketing amenity-rich rental communities across growth markets. It blends professional operations, resident-experience programming, and a digital leasing journey to drive occupancy and retention. The brand treats renting as a lifestyle relationship, not a transaction.
Modern.scope: A multifamily operating-brand and resident-experience system covering wordmark, community sub-brand framework, leasing-center and signage identity, resident-app brand layer, and amenity branding. The work defines a warm, lifestyle-driven voice for renters and a performance voice for owners.
Modern.brandNameRationale: 'Vesta', the Roman goddess of hearth and home, evokes warmth, belonging, and the heart of the household. It signals apartments designed to feel like home, not just housing.
Modern.industrySummary: Multifamily in 2025 is digesting a historic supply wave: a 50-year-high in new apartment deliveries, concentrated in Sun Belt markets, pushed rent growth to near-flat and elevated concessions as operators compete for renters. Occupancy held up on resilient renter demand fueled by unaffordable for-sale housing, but operators now win on retention, experience, and operational efficiency rather than rent hikes. Renters-by-necessity and lifestyle renters both expect amenities, digital leasing, and responsive service.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Greystar (greystar.com) is the largest apartment operator globally; AvalonBay (avalonbay.com) and Equity Residential (equityapartments.com) operate premium communities. Vesta Living differs by leaning into resident-experience programming and a cohesive lifestyle brand across communities, competing on retention and belonging rather than scale alone.
Modern.positioningStatement: For renters who want a home, not a unit, Vesta Living operates communities designed around belonging and service.
Modern.positioningRationale: In an oversupplied, concession-heavy market, retention is the decisive economic lever, and experience drives retention. A belonging-focused lifestyle brand differentiates commodity apartments and reduces costly turnover.

targetAudience.primary: Renters aged 24-45, from young professionals to lifestyle renters and renters-by-necessity priced out of buying. They value amenities, location, community, and seamless digital service, and they research communities heavily on reviews and tours. They renew based on experience and responsiveness, and they expect app-based leasing, payments, and maintenance.

Modern.brandDescription: Eventide Commons develops and operates 55+ and senior living communities spanning active-adult, independent living, and assisted living. It designs for dignity, connection, and wellness, with hospitality-grade service and care that scales with residents' needs. The brand reframes senior living as a vibrant chapter, not a last resort.
Modern.scope: A senior-living brand system covering wordmark, community sub-brand framework, sales-gallery experience, wayfinding and signage, family and resident collateral, and a care-continuum identity. The work defines a warm, dignified, trustworthy voice for seniors and their adult children.
Modern.brandNameRationale: 'Eventide' poetically evokes the golden, graceful hours of evening, a dignified metaphor for later life; 'Commons' signals shared community and belonging. Together it conveys a warm, communal, dignified place.
Modern.industrySummary: Senior living in 2025 stands at the front edge of a demographic wave: the 80+ population is climbing sharply as the oldest baby boomers age, while new-supply construction slowed after pandemic-era headwinds, tightening occupancy and improving operator pricing power. Demand recovered strongly post-COVID, with active-adult and wellness-forward independent living growing fastest. Adult-child decision-makers increasingly weigh hospitality, technology, and care quality, and labor costs remain the operators' central challenge.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Brookdale Senior Living (brookdale.com) is the largest US operator; Atria Senior Living (atriaseniorliving.com) emphasizes vibrant lifestyle; Erickson Senior Living (ericksonseniorliving.com) runs large continuing-care campuses. Eventide Commons differs by leading with wellness, design, and a seamless care continuum, positioning vibrancy and dignity over institutional care imagery.
Modern.positioningStatement: For older adults and the families who love them, Eventide Commons is the community designed for living well, with care that grows as needs do.
Modern.positioningRationale: Adult children fear institutional, undignified care; leading with wellness, design, and dignity directly addresses the emotional decision. A seamless care continuum removes the fear of disruptive moves, a top concern in the category.

Seniors value independence, dignity, social connection, and wellness; adult children prioritize safety, care quality, and peace of mind. Both research extensively, tour multiple communities, and decide emotionally on the feel of the place and trust in the staff.

Modern.brandDescription: Quad & Co. develops and operates purpose-built student housing near major universities, offering by-the-bed leases, study-and-social amenities, and a frictionless digital experience. It is built for the rhythms of student life, academic calendars, roommate matching, and parent guarantors. The brand balances fun, focus, and reliability for students and the parents who pay.
Modern.scope: A student-housing brand system covering wordmark, property sub-brand framework, leasing-and-tour identity, resident-app brand layer, amenity branding, and a parent-facing trust layer. The work defines an energetic student voice and a reassuring parent voice.
Modern.brandNameRationale: 'Quad' is the iconic campus courtyard and the heart of student social life, plus a nod to four-roommate units. It instantly signals university living and community.
Modern.industrySummary: Purpose-built student housing in 2025 is a standout asset class: pre-leasing velocity hit record highs and rent growth outpaced conventional multifamily, driven by enrollment concentration at large flagship universities and chronic undersupply of beds near campus. Investors favor the sector's recession-resilience and parent-backed leases. Students now expect high-speed connectivity, study spaces, wellness amenities, and fully digital, by-the-bed leasing with roommate matching.
Modern.competitorLandscape: American Campus Communities (americancampus.com) is the largest student-housing owner; Landmark Properties (landmark-properties.com) develops premium 'The Standard' and 'The Retreat' brands; Core Spaces (corespaces.com) builds amenity-rich communities. Quad & Co. differs by pairing a strong student lifestyle brand with a transparent, reassuring parent-guarantor experience and academic-success amenities.
Modern.positioningStatement: For students who want campus life done right and parents who want peace of mind, Quad & Co. delivers housing built for both.
Modern.positioningRationale: Student housing has two buyers, the student who chooses and the parent who pays and guarantees; serving both explicitly is differentiating. Pairing lifestyle appeal with parent reassurance addresses the real decision dynamic the category often ignores.

targetAudience.primary: Undergraduate students aged 18-23 at large universities, plus their parents who co-sign and often fund the lease. Students value social life, amenities, location to campus, and a fully digital experience; parents value safety, transparency, and a hassle-free guarantor process. Leasing decisions happen early (often a year ahead), socially (with roommate groups), and with parental sign-off.

Modern.tagline: Your room. Our city. One key.
Modern.brandDescription: Threshold Co-Living operates fully-furnished, all-inclusive co-living homes in high-cost cities, offering private rooms with shared common spaces, flexible terms, and built-in community. One membership covers rent, utilities, furniture, cleaning, and Wi-Fi. The brand is built for mobile young professionals who want affordability, flexibility, and instant belonging in expensive cities.
Modern.scope: A co-living brand system covering wordmark, house sub-brand framework, member-app brand layer, community-programming identity, and leasing/onboarding collateral. The work defines a warm, design-forward, community-driven voice.
Modern.brandNameRationale: 'Threshold' marks the doorway you cross into a new home and a new community, and the moment of arrival in a new city. It evokes welcome, transition, and belonging.
Modern.industrySummary: Co-living in 2025 is rebounding as an affordability and flexibility answer to record urban rents and stretched young-professional budgets. After a pandemic dip, demand recovered strongly among remote workers, relocators, and singles seeking community amid an isolation epidemic; all-inclusive, flexible-lease models gained traction where studio rents are prohibitive. Investors and operators favor co-living's higher per-square-foot yields, while design quality and genuine community programming separate winners from glorified hostels.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Common (common.com) and Outpost Club (outpostclub.com) operate co-living across US cities; Habyt (habyt.com) scales co-living globally. Threshold differs by pairing genuinely designed, hospitality-grade homes with intentional community programming and radically simple all-in pricing, avoiding the cramped, transactional feel of budget operators.
Modern.positioningStatement: For young professionals priced out of going it alone, Threshold Co-Living offers a furnished room, an all-in price, and a built-in community, one key away.
Modern.positioningRationale: Urban affordability and loneliness are the twin drivers; solving both with all-in pricing and real community is a sharp, dual value prop. Simplicity (one membership, everything included) cuts through the friction of traditional leases that mobile renters resent.

targetAudience.primary: Mobile professionals aged 22-34, including recent grads, relocators, and remote workers, living in expensive cities. They are budget-conscious, community-seeking, and value flexibility and convenience over space and permanence. They want to move in fast with zero furniture hassle, meet people quickly, and avoid year-long leases and utility setup.

Modern.tagline: Homes for the people who keep cities running.
Modern.brandDescription: Keystone Workforce Housing develops and preserves affordable and workforce rental housing for essential workers, teachers, nurses, and service employees, through LIHTC, public-private partnerships, and mission-driven capital. It builds quality, dignified housing at attainable rents near jobs and transit. The brand champions housing as the foundation of stable communities.
Modern.scope: A mission-driven development brand covering wordmark, community identity, resident and partner collateral, capital-stack and impact-reporting templates, and a public-affairs/advocacy voice. The work defines a credible, dignified, civic voice for residents, public partners, and investors.
Modern.brandNameRationale: 'Keystone' is the central stone that holds an arch together, a fitting metaphor for housing that holds communities together, and for the essential workers it serves. It signals foundational, structural importance.
Modern.industrySummary: Affordable and workforce housing in 2025 faces acute demand against a national shortage of millions of affordable units, as record rents outpace essential-worker wages and the 'missing middle' of households earning 60-120% of area median income is squeezed hardest. Higher interest rates and construction costs strained deal feasibility, raising the importance of LIHTC, tax-exempt bonds, and public-private subsidy. Policy momentum and ESG-driven impact capital expanded funding sources even as the supply gap widened.
Modern.competitorLandscape: The Michaels Organization (themichaelsorg.com) and McCormack Baron Salazar (mccormackbaron.com) lead affordable development; Related Affordable (relatedaffordable.com) preserves and builds at scale. Keystone differs by focusing on the underserved workforce band (essential workers above strict affordable thresholds) and pairing development with transparent community-impact reporting.
Modern.positioningStatement: For the essential workers cities can't run without, Keystone Workforce Housing builds dignified, attainable homes where they're needed most.
Modern.positioningRationale: Framing around essential workers reframes affordable housing from charity to civic necessity, broadening political and investor support. Focusing on the squeezed 'missing middle' addresses a real, underserved band between subsidized and market-rate housing.

targetAudience.primary: Three audiences: essential-worker households (teachers, nurses, first responders, service staff) earning 60-120% of AMI; public partners and housing agencies; and mission-driven and ESG investors. Residents need quality, attainable homes near work; public partners need credible execution; investors need both returns and measurable impact. All reward transparency, dignity, and demonstrated community benefit.
